messages.subject: Scatter between 2 data frames
parts:

I need to plot scatter plot for all variables (in one graph) between df1 and df2 and add R and p-value to the graph. the desired output will be like the attached image:


Has anyone worked on such thing?
Thanks in advance,
Bic

parts:
If you want something a little jazzier, you can try this:

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
df1 = data.frame(sales=sales,profit=profit) %>% gather( key = metric, value = money, 1:2)

df2 = data.frame(sales=sales,profit=profit) %>% gather( key = metric2, value = money2, 1:2)

df3 = cbind(df1, df2)

ggplot(data=df3, aes(x = money, y = money2)) + geom_point() + facet_grid(.~metric)

parts:
this is easy with a for loop:

vars <- names(df1)

for (var in vars){
    plot(df1[,var] , df2[,var], main=var)
}

You can add the R^2 and P-value calculations to the loop, and of course you can switch my plot code with Rosie's much prettier plot code.

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Scatter between 2 data frames
parts:
To calculate p-values:

library(plyr)

pr2 = ddply(df3, .(metric), summarize, R2 = summary(lm(money~money2))$r.squared, p = summary(lm(money~money2))$coefficients[2,4])

#add it to your plot
ggplot(data=df3) + geom_point( aes(x = money, y = money2)) + facet_grid(.~metric) +
  geom_text(data = pr2, aes(label = paste("R2=", R2, "p=", p), x = 5.5, y = 5.5), size = 8)

On Tue, Mar 7, 2017 at 10:03 PM, Rosemary Hartman <roseh...@gmail.com> wrote:
To calculate p-values:

library(plyr)

pr2 = ddply(df3, .(metric), summarize, R2 = summary(lm(money~money2))$r.squared, p = summary(lm(money~money2))$coefficients[2,4])

#add it to your plot
ggplot(data=df3) + geom_point( aes(x = money, y = money2)) + facet_grid(.~metric) +
  geom_text(data = pr2, aes(label = paste("R2=", R2, "p=", p), x = 5.5, y = 5.5), size = 8)


On Tue, Mar 7, 2017 at 11:12 AM, Rosemary Hartman <roseh...@gmail.com> wrote:
If you want something a little jazzier, you can try this:

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
sales = c(1,4,3,2,3,4,5,6,7,6,7,5)
profit = c(4,3,2,3,4,5,6,7,7,7,6,5)
df1 = data.frame(sales=sales,profit=profit) %>% gather( key = metric, value = money, 1:2)

sales = c(1,4,3,2,3,4,5,6,7,6,7,5)
profit = c(4,3,2,3,4,5,6,7,7,7,6,5)
df2 = data.frame(sales=sales,profit=profit) %>% gather( key = metric2, value = money2, 1:2)

df3 = cbind(df1, df2)

ggplot(data=df3, aes(x = money, y = money2)) + geom_point() + facet_grid(.~metric)
